subject: Food Science
title: Aseptic Processing
description: A quick, practical guide to Aseptic Processing.

hook.text: Juice boxes sit on shelves for months without refrigeration. They're not canned—they're aseptically processed.

buildup.text: Aseptic processing sterilizes the food and the package separately, then fills the package in a sterile environment.

discovery.text: Food is flash-sterilized at ultra-high temperatures for seconds, then cooled instantly—minimal flavor and nutrient damage.

twist.text: Aseptic packaging allows lightweight cartons instead of heavy cans—reducing shipping weight by 70% and cutting costs.

climax.text: Tetra Pak pioneered aseptic cartons in 1961. Today, 190 billion Tetra Pak packages are produced annually.

punchline.text: Sterilize the food. Sterilize the box. Combine them in a sterile room. Done.

quiz.question: What makes aseptic processing different from canning?
options: It uses chemicals instead of heat
Food and packaging are sterilized separately then combined in a sterile environment
